Title: Toward Interpretable Topic Discovery via Anchored Correlation Explanation
In this workshop paper, we introduce a simple approach to anchored information theoretic topic modeling using a novel combination of Correlation Explanation (CorEx) (Ver Steeg & Galstyan, 2014) and the information bottle- neck (Tishby et al., 2000). This ﬂexible framework enables the user to leverage domain knowledge to guide exploration of a collection of documents and to impose semantics onto latent factors learned by CorEx.

answer: The paper incorporates expert knowledge by letting users specify a set of "anchored" relevance variables—fuzzy and informal expert-provided words or domain knowledge—so that latent topics are optimized to be informative both about correlations in the data and about those expert-specified anchors [7]. This anchored approach builds on a combination of the information bottleneck and Total Correlation Explanation (CorEx), enabling users to impose semantics onto the latent factors learned by CorEx and guide exploration of a document collection [1][7]. Like seeded LDA, this allows the specification of word–topic relationships [6].
